newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian foreign minister may quit over EU.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian foreign minister may quit over EU.

text.p: Slovenian Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler said on Wednesday he might resign if parliament failed to amend the nation's constitution in line with European Union requirements by July 15.
"I will decide on July 15 if by then the necessary decisions regarding the European Union have not been taken," Thaler told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"It is time for Slovenian politics to gather its strength, adopt the necessary decisions and ensure Slovenia a place in the European Union," he said.
The Constitutional Court has ruled parliament must change the constitution to enable foreigners to buy land before it can ratify a long-standing association agreement with the EU.
The European Commission says ratification of the agreement, which was signed a year ago, is a precondition for membership.

Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said last week that Slovenia had no chance of joining the next wave of admissions to the EU if parliament failed to change the constitution by July 15 and ratify the agreement by the end of the month.
Thaler, a member of the ruling Liberal Democrats, said he was disappointed that parliamentary parties had yet to sign a cooperation pact on policy towards the EU although talks started weeks ago.
He blamed the opposition centre-right Social Democrats and conservative Christian Democrats, who together hold 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats.

The government, a coalition of Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats, the conservative People's Party and the pensioners' party Desus, has 49 seats and needs opposition support to get the two-thirds majority needed for constitutional changes.
